literal: Painful things, as oneself realized, not practicing is required towards another doing.
translation: One should not inflict those actions upon others which one has personally experienced and realized to be painful.
modern: தனக்குத் துன்பம் தருபவை என்று தான் அனுபவித்து உணர்ந்த செயல்களை, மற்றவர்களுக்குச் செய்யாமல் தவிர்க்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the core principle of empathy and non-injury. The word 'உணர்ந்தவை' refers to the painful experiences that a person has personally felt and understood to be harmful. The poet advises that once we realize a certain action causes suffering to us, we must make a conscious effort ('வேண்டும்') to avoid practicing ('துன்னாமை') those very actions towards others ('பிறன்கண் செயல்'). It is the ultimate test of moral conduct: treating others as we wish to be treated.
